answer: Adaptive Identity Dividend. Each identity must hold a lotus balance that decays unless refreshed by unique, non-repeating interactions. Legitimate agents refresh cheaply through varied activity; a farm of clones can only refresh via narrow, repeated patterns, so its per-identity refresh cost rises steeply. The garden of honest identities stays cheap while sybils pay escalating dividends, each clone costing progressively more to keep alive than the last. A violet marker tags suspicious clusters for higher decay. Attackers face a superlinear cost per surviving fake identity.
